podcast.title: Pedestrian Accident (2001) – Hit Man at 50 mph on Las Vegas Freeway, Outcome Unknown
podcast.body: In 2001, Brandon Flowers was driving in the Las Vegas area when a drunk pedestrian walked into his lane on the freeway. Despite honking and braking, he struck the man at approximately 50 mph. The pedestrian hit the windshield and his shoes flew off. Police questioned Brandon and released him. He has never found out whether the man survived. In a *GQ* interview he described it as "terrible" and "pretty traumatic." Brandon rarely discusses the incident. "Did he recover? Or is the singer of the Killers really a killer?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alt Rock Resurgence of 2004
podcast.body: The Killers were named as one of the new and exciting bands contributing to the resurgence of Alt Rock by 2004. "By 2004, Alt Rock was back with all kinds of new exciting bands that was Franz Ferdinand and Modest Mouse and the Killers and Billy Towns and the Stills and Jet, the Ye-Yaz and Hot Hot Heat."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Intentional Springsteen Influence on Sam's Town (2006)
podcast.body: Singer Brandon Flowers openly stated that The Killers deliberately aimed to make their "Sam's Town" album "as Springsteen as possible," striving for big American rock songs featuring horn sections and rich storytelling. "Singer Brandon Flowers was totally honest when he said the group went into this album with the idea of making it as Springsteen as possible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sam's Town Tour Rider (2006) – Day-Specific Alcohol Requirements
podcast.body: The Killers' rider had very specific alcohol requirements that varied depending on the day of the week. On Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, they demanded Makers Mark bourbon and Absolut vodka. For Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays, the bourbon had to be Jack Daniels, and they also required some kind of gin. On Sundays, only a bottle of Jameson's Irish whiskey would suffice. Additionally, each night required large cases of Corona, Coors, a premium beer, cider, and a couple of bottles of unspecified red wine. "If the gig was on a Sunday, only a bottle of Jameson's Irish whiskey would do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sam's Town Tour Rider (2006) – Standard Provisions
podcast.body: The rider for the "Sam's Town" tour included fairly standard requests such as chocolate bars (Snickers, Kit Kat), a deli tray sufficient for 20 people with sliced cheese, crackers, white bread, and fresh fruits and vegetables, including six fresh avocados. "a selection of chocolate bars, Snickers, Kit Kat and so on a deli tray enough to feed 20 people with a commensurate amount of sliced cheese, crackers, and white bread, also some fruits and veggies, and six fresh avocados."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performance with Springsteen at Pinkpop Festival (2009)
podcast.body: The Killers performed with Bruce Springsteen at the 2009 Pinkpop Festival in the Netherlands, with Brandon Flowers joining Springsteen and the E Street Band on stage to sing "Thunder Road" after The Killers' own set. "The killers played right before Springsteen, and Brandon was brought back on during the East Street band set to sing Thunder Road."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Publishing Rights Sale to Eldridge Industries (Prior to 2020)
podcast.body: The Killers sold the publishing rights to all their songs created from their formation until 2020 to Eldridge Industries, a company that invests in various sectors including insurance, real estate, and music. The exact price was not revealed, but it is speculated to be in excess of $100 million due to the enduring popularity and high streaming numbers of their music. This lump sum payment offers tax advantages, being treated as a capital gain rather than income, and provides financial security for the band, allowing them to continue making new music and touring while Eldridge focuses on maximizing catalog revenue. "Eldridge Industries and they invested everything from insurance to real estate to music. So how much did they pay the killers for all those songs released prior to 2020? No idea because the price was never revealed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Mr. Brightside" Unstoppable Momentum
podcast.body: The massive popularity of "Mr. Brightside" is attributed to various factors, including The Killers' strong touring presence in the UK, its frequent play at parties, sporting events, and on television, and its ubiquitous presence on music charts and streaming platforms, which generated "unstoppable momentum." "Maybe it's the ubiquity on the charts and streaming platforms, which has given it unstoppable momentum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 6: (50-41)

podcast.title: "Mr. Brightside" Video Success
podcast.body: Two videos were produced for "Mr. Brightside"; the official color video has accumulated approximately 600 million views. When combined with other separate video postings of the song, total viewership exceeds one billion. "The official video, the one shot in color, which has been seen about 600 million times, added in the other separate video postings of the song and were up over a billion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 6: (50-41)

podcast.title: "Mr. Brightside" as a Coping Mechanism
podcast.body: After seeing his ex-girlfriend with another man, Brandon Flowers immediately left the bar but couldn't shake the image from his mind. He then spiraled into imagining what they would be doing later that night, writing everything down on a pad of paper in an attempt to convince himself to put on a brave face, hence calling himself "Mr. Brightside." "He wrote everything out on a pad of paper hoping to convince himself to put on a brave face with the situation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Sam's Town" Album Title Origin
podcast.body: The Killers' album "Sam's Town" derives its name from the Sam's Town Hotel and Gambling Hall, a casino located in their hometown of Las Vegas. Bassist Mark Stoermer held a personal connection to this landmark, as he could see the casino's sign from his bedroom when he was young. "It's the title is taken from a casino in the band's hometown of Las Vegas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The Killers are considered a genuine 21st-century superstar rock act, demonstrating traits like strong consensus and significant commercial success. "There is a genuine 21st century superstar rock act."

podcast.title: 80s-Style Keyboards
podcast.body: The Killers, alongside The Bravery, were credited with bringing 80s-style keyboards back into vogue in rock music during the mid-2000s. Their sound contributed to a broader palette of styles emerging in the alt-rock universe. "The bravery and the killers brought the sound of 80-style keyboards back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Anton Corbijn's Vision for "Sam's Town" Cover
podcast.body: Photographer Anton Corbijn, a renowned artist who has collaborated with U2, Depeche Mode, and many others, rejected The Killers' initial concept for their "Sam's Town" cover, which they described as a "chic gypsy look." Corbijn instead proposed an aesthetic of "tired and faded glory," bringing to life this vision with elements such as a beat-up camper trailer, a stuffed big-horned desert sheep, and the model Felice LaZae. "When presented with the project, he overruled the band's desire for something they described as a chic gypsy look."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Attention and Sales Translation
podcast.body: The Killers represent an instance where mass consensus has translated into music sales and concert attendance similar to those seen with the biggest bands of previous eras, unlike many other contemporary acts. "But like we saw with the killers, this does not mean there are instances of mass consensus that look a lot like the old days."

podcast.title: Brandon Flowers' Personal Inspiration
podcast.body: The genesis of "Mr. Brightside" came from a deeply personal experience for singer Brandon Flowers. As a 19-year-old, he was living in Las Vegas with his sister, renting a room for $200 a month, and was heartbroken after walking into The Crown and Anchor bar and seeing his ex-girlfriend, his first serious relationship, with another man. This betrayal inspired the song's narrative. "Somewhere at the root of all this, at all these achievements and profits is a real woman."

podcast.title: Crude Demo's Role in Record Deal
podcast.body: The initial composition of "Mr. Brightside" involved Brandon Flowers writing the lyrics over music already composed by guitarist Dave Keuning. They then created a crude demo using a drum machine, and this early version of the song was instrumental in helping the full Killers lineup secure their first record deal. "When the full killer's lineup came together, this was one of the songs that landed them a record deal."

podcast.title: Early Songwriting Success
podcast.body: "Mr. Brightside" was one of the first three songs ever written by The Killers, proving to be an almost instant success that helped launch their career and secure a record deal. Its massive popularity and enduring presence are remarkable for such an early composition. "It's not bad considering it was one of the first three songs the band ever wrote."

podcast.body: An unnamed song from "Sam's Town," heavily influenced by Bruce Springsteen's "Born to Run," received a Grammy nomination in the category of Best Rock Song. "The result was a single that was nominated for a Grammy in the category of Best Rock Song."

podcast.title: Indie Rock Revival Post 9/11
podcast.body: The Killers were part of the indie rock revival that saw rock's popularity begin to rise again in the wake of the 9/11 attacks and subsequent American military interventions in Iraq and Afghanistan. "I don't think the strokes and the A.A.S and the white stripes and the killers."

podcast.title: Influence from Interpol
podcast.body: The Killers were identified as one of the "likeminded groups" that experienced an immediate influence from Interpol's debut record, "Turn on the Bright Lights," released in 2002. "There was a little Interpol in everyone from the killers to the XX."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence from The Strokes
podcast.body: After hearing The Strokes' debut album "Is This It," a young band from Las Vegas called The Killers reportedly became "depressed." They subsequently discarded all their ongoing work and "started from scratch," with only one song, "Mr. Brightside," surviving this creative overhaul. The influence of The Strokes can be heard in the construction and recording of that song. "A young band from Las Vegas called the Killers, heard the album, got depressed, and then throughout everything that they were doing and started from scratch."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence of David Bowie
podcast.body: The Killers' sound and vision contain "bits of Bowie DNA," indicating a clear influence from David Bowie's work. "Nirvana, the sex pistols, the food fighters, nine inch nails, REM smashing pumpkins, the killers, Scott Wyland, Coldplay. They all have bits of Bowie DNA in their sound and vision."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on The Struts
podcast.body: The Killers were cited as one of the influences on the British band The Struts, along with Queen, Aerosmith, Oasis, and The Rolling Stones. This reflects a trend of new young bands drawing inspiration from old school classic rock and iconic acts. "A British band brought up on Queen, Aerosmith Oasis, the killers and the Rolling Stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Reception and Re-evaluation of Sam's Town
podcast.body: Upon its release, "Sam's Town" initially received unfavorable reviews, prompting the band to pivot musically. However, over time, the album has been re-evaluated, with a modern consensus acknowledging its Springsteen influence, though suggesting a non-repeat of this direct homage. "The reviews weren't great at first, and the band ended up moving in a different direction, which worked out fine, of course. But in the years since Samstown has been out, there has been a considerable amount of re-evaluation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for "Mr. Brightside"
podcast.body: The song was directly inspired by a real event where singer Brandon Flowers walked into a bar in Las Vegas and saw his old girlfriend with a new partner. The identity of the woman remains unknown, but she inadvertently became responsible for one of the most enduring singles of the century. "Singer Brandon Flowers walked into a bar at his hometown of Las Vegas and saw an old girlfriend with a new guy."

podcast.title: Planned Woodstock 50 Performance
podcast.body: The Killers were among the 80 artists announced to perform at the Woodstock 50 festival, which aimed to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Woodstock in August 2019. Despite the star-studded lineup, the festival was eventually canceled. "80 artists had originally signed up, including Santana, Dead & Company, The Killers, Jay-Z, Imagine Dragons, Cage the Elf and Miley Cyrus, Vampire Weekend, and more."

podcast.title: Return from Hiatus
podcast.body: After a considerable number of years, the group released a new album, putting to rest speculation that they had separated or retired. "Ya llegamos a pensar que el grupo se había separado o que se había retirado, pero después de bastantes años sacan nuevo disco."

On Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, the rider requested Makers Mark Whiskey and Absolute Vodka, while on Sundays, it specified Tequila and Jameson's Irish Whiskey. podcast.title: The Crown and Anchor Bar Encounter
podcast.body: Brandon Flowers' painful encounter that inspired "Mr. Brightside" occurred when he walked into The Crown and Anchor bar in Las Vegas and saw his ex-girlfriend with another man. He had been trying to avoid her to prevent such a situation, but his fears were realized that day. "One day he walked into a bar called the Crown and Anchor and sitting there having a drink was his girlfriend. Actually, it was his ex-girlfriend and the person involved in Brandon's first proper, serious relationship. She was there with another dude."

podcast.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
podcast.body: The Killers contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

xref.title: Immense Influence on New Rock
xref.body: David Bowie is considered uniquely influential in the world of New Rock, with his work in the 1970s being traceable as a root for genres like punk, new wave, industrial, and electronic music. His influence is evident in the sound and vision of numerous bands including Nirvana, the Sex Pistols, Foo Fighters, Nine Inch Nails, R.E.M., Smashing Pumpkins, The Killers, Scott Weiland, and Coldplay. He is described as "the Beatles of the alt rock set." "Take any genre of rock you like punk, new wave, industrial electronic and somehow you'll be able to trace it back to something that David Bowie did in the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Indie Rock Revival Post 9/11
xref.body: The Strokes were among the bands that drove an indie rock revival following the world events of 9/11 and the American invasion of Iraq and Afghanistan, contributing to a period when rock music began to rise in popularity again. "After 9-11 and the American invasion of Iraq and Afghanistan, Happy music no longer seemed appropriate. This popularity began to rise again, driven by an indie rock revival. I don't think the strokes and the A.A.S and the white stripes and the killers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

xref.title: Influence on Alt-Rock Icons
xref.body: Despite his humble beginnings with The Shades, Lou Reed later became a foundational influence on many significant artists in the alt-rock scene. His work inspired figures such as David Bowie, Iggy Pop, R.E.M., and The Killers. "he would later influence Bowie and Iggy and R.E.M. and the killers and so many of the other movers and shakers of the alt-rock scene in the decades ahead."

xref.title: Influence on Other Bands
xref.body: The Strokes, particularly with their debut album "Is This It," profoundly influenced many bands that followed, making them one of the most important bands of the 2000s. Kings of Leon learned to play by emulating "Is This It." The Killers, after hearing the album, reportedly scrapped all their existing material except for "Mr. Brightside" and restarted, with elements of The Strokes' construction and recording audible in their music. Other bands like Arctic Monkeys, Franz Ferdinand, and LCD Sound System also credit The Strokes as an influence. "If it wasn't for the Strokes, it's possible that the Indy Rock Garage Rock Revival that took hold in New York City in the early 2000s wouldn't have grown the way it did."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
